newsitem.title: USA: "Batman & Robin" bitten by box office competition.
newsitem.headline: "Batman & Robin" bitten by box office competition.

text.p: "Batman & Robin," the fourth installment in the lucrative Caped Crusader franchise, flew into the top of the weekend box office with $43.6 million, according to studio estimates released Sunday.
However, the Friday to Sunday take was only the third best of the four Batman movies, surpassing the $40.49 million opening of the first "Batman" in June 1989.
The record is held by "Batman Forever," which opened to $52.78 million in June 1995, while "Batman Returns" scored $45.69 million in June 1992.

"Batman & Robin," which marks the debut of George Clooney as the masked crime fighter, played on 2,934 screens for an average of $14,860, the lowest of the four Batman movies. The previous low was the $17,820 for "Batman Returns."
However, Warner Bros., which released the movie, said it was pleased with the numbers for "Batman & Robin," and noted that it was the seventh biggest opening of all time.

Barry Reardon, the studio's president of distribution, predicted the movie would earn $150 million domestically, and would perform strongly overseas where Arnold Schwarzenegger is a huge draw. Schwarzenegger, who has top billing in the movie over Clooney, plays the villain Mr. Freeze.
Reardon also said that "Batman & Robin," unlike its three predecessors, faced strong competition from action pictures, in this case "Con Air," "The Lost World" and "Speed 2."
Even the second-placed romantic comedy, "My Best Friend's Wedding," which opened to $21.5 million, probably took about $4-$5 million from "Batman & Robin," he estimated.
"My Best Friend's Wedding" sets a new opening record for a romantic comedy, and is also the best opening for its star, Julia Roberts, according to TriStar Pictures.
The previous record for a romantic comedy was held by "Sleepless in Seattle," which opened to $17.2 million in June 1993, and went on to earn $126 million.

Roberts' previous best was "The Pelican Brief," which opened to $16.9 million in December 1993, and went on to earn $100.7 million. Her most successful movie, 1990's "Pretty Woman," opened to $11.28 million and finished up with $178 million.
"It's probably the first picture of the summer that's not action-oriented or mega-budgeted that will do over $100 million," said a spokesman for TriStar.
He said the movie played "sensationally" to women and "very well" to men.

The Nicolas Cage airborne thriller, "Con Air," slipped a notch to third in its third weekend, with $10.2 million, which takes its overall total to $67.7 million. It averaged $3,468 from 2,941 screens, an increase of 112 screens.

Steven Spielberg's "The Lost World: Jurassic Park," also fell a notch, to fourth, with $8.0 million. After 32 days in release, the dinosaur extravaganza's total is $204.9 million, placing it 20th on the list of all-time domestic grossers. It averaged $2,597 from 3,080 screens.

Last weekend's number one, "Speed 2: Cruise Control," tumbled to fifth with $7.2 million. The 10-day total for the critically maligned Sandra Bullock action movie is $30.7 million. Its 55 percent drop was the third biggest in the top 10. Its average was $2,746 from 2,622 screens.

"Batman & Robin" is released by Warner Bros, a unit of Time Warner Inc.. "My Best Friend's Wedding" is released by TriStar Pictures, a unit of Sony Corp.. "Con Air" is released by Walt Disney Co.. "The Lost World: Jurassic Park" is released by Universal Pictures, a unit of Seagram Co. Ltd.. "Speed 2: Cruise Control" is released by 20th Century Fox, a unit of News Corp..
